audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: Karma wins 41.18% over 68 games while the content chart gave her 6 of 7 stages. The full layer said Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ekko/Skill/Ekko, so the two layers also disagreed on four rows.
audit.why: Karma's edge is levels 1-3, where Ekko has one 9s Timewinder and a 325-range Phase Dive. From level 4 his Timewinder actually out-ranges her — 1075 against her 950 — so that row is a genuine skill window, and from 6 onward Chronobreak, then his item spike, then a 50s rank-3 Chronobreak decide it.
audit.corrected: Both layers now read Karma/Karma/Karma/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko, with the whys and whys[] on every moved row rewritten to match.
sources: brief.packet winRate 41.18 / 68 games and the levelChart defect
brief.enemyKit Ekko Q range 1075 cd 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, E range 325

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why read 'No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank... press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up' on a row already marked Ekko, and two content fields hedged with 'generally'.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 but 50s at rank 3 — an unusually steep rank curve, and the reason the late game runs away from Karma rather than staying even.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[6].why, spikes[2].text and spikes[3].text now state the 110s-to-50s curve with no hedge.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and described Chronobreak only as 'erases your kill and bursts back'. All three of the brief's missingInteractions were absent from the page.
audit.why: Chronobreak makes Ekko untargetable and heals him for a percentage of the damage received in that window — so a commit dumped into it is refunded twice over, and Grievous Wounds is what makes chip stick. Phase Dive is an auto-attack reset that teleports him to the target, so the attack wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Parallel Convergence is 22/20/18/16/14s at 1600 range and its anomaly appears seconds before it stuns, which is the dodge.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad, dosFull[1].d, report[5].t, breakdown.feeding and breakdown.late now carry the untargetable-plus-heal behaviour, the anti-heal timing, the Phase Dive wind-up tell, and the real numbers.
sources: brief.enemyKit Ekko R text and flags untargetable/heal
brief.enemyKit Ekko E autoReset flag and text

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged wants.foe[1] 'Use Chronobreak' and wants.foe[2] 'Drive Resonance' as probable wrong names.
audit.why: Chronobreak is the correct name for Ekko's R, and wants.foe[2] already reads 'Z-Drive Resonance' in full — the matcher clipped the string. Both are false positives; no edits made.

edits.before: Right at level 6 you need to be careful — Chronobreak lets him rewind out of a bad trade and punish you if you overextend chasing what looks like a kill, so don't get greedy the moment he hits his ultimate. Past that single spike, though, your range and shields still let you control the pace even once he completes his first item; his stun-into-combo is real damage but you can disengage before he lands the full sequence if you're not caught out of position. Keep playing at range and punish his short trading windows rather than letting him dictate the fight. This phase stays broadly in your favor outside that level 6 window.
edits.after: Right at level 6 the lane changes hands — Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 and makes him untargetable while it heals a share of the damage you just dealt, so a commit that looked lethal simply refunds him. Never spend your last spell into the rewind; wait for him to land and W-root him there. Once he completes his first item the Parallel Convergence stun into a full combo is lethal rather than painful, and you own no dash to leave it — only a 10s Soul Shield, which has to be up before he arrives. Play at 950, punish the 22s anomaly window, and take plates instead of duels.

edits.before: The late game stays close to even — Ekko's teamfight combo and ability to reset a fight with his ult give him real threat potential, but your poke and Mantra shields keep you from ever being clearly outclassed. Play around cooldowns, hold shields for his stun attempt, and don't isolate yourself where his combo can catch you alone. This is a lane where careful play keeps you ahead rather than one you can coast through on stats alone.
edits.after: Late, Chronobreak drops to 50s at rank 3 and he re-enters every fight he loses, healing a share of what he took — so chip damage alone never finishes him. Buy Grievous Wounds and hold it for the rewind. Play as pure peel: shield whoever he stuns, W-root him the instant he lands, and never stand alone where Phase Dive reaches you with nobody to root him off. This phase is his unless your team punishes the window while his ult is down.

notes:
CHART: packet-flagged — 41.18% over 68 games against a content chart giving Karma 6 of 7 stages, and the two layers disagreed on four rows. Both now read Karma/Karma/Karma/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko. Rows 0,1,2,5 were full-side edits (content already held the value or was moved alongside); rows 3,4,6 were content win[N] edits where the full side already held the target. Every why and whys[] on a moved row was rewritten in the same proposal.

NOTABLE: Ekko's Timewinder is 1075 range against Karma's 950 Q. The page repeatedly claimed Karma out-ranges him. She does not from level 4 on, and that is why row 3 is a skill window rather than hers.

All three missingInteractions landed: the untargetable-plus-heal Chronobreak (do not dump the last spell), Grievous Wounds timing, and the Phase Dive attack wind-up as the tell.

SuspectNames: both flags are false positives — 'Chronobreak' is correct and wants.foe[2] already reads 'Z-Drive Resonance' in full.

SCOPE: I held to two report[] edits (report[0].t and report[5].t). That leaves report[1].t and report[3].t still carrying the old winCon / tradeGood / tradeBad strings verbatim, so they will read stale against the rewritten versions. They are the next two to sync if the cap is lifted.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Karma's Focused Resolve tether breaks when Ekko becomes untargetable through Chronobreak, and whether Parallel Convergence's stun is reduced by tenacity. Neither is in Riot's text.
